messages:
marta: heads up — we need to codify the degradation paths for the continuous batcher before the refactor lands. currently behavior is implicit and awkward under heavy multi-tenant load

sam: totally. can we enumerate the visible states first? e.g. normal coalesce -> microqueue fallback -> per-tenant shed -> reject. keep it small and composable. :+1:

kevin: adding: degraded-quantized lanes (low-precision) as an intermediate step. helps keep latency but trades quality. but the current admission API doesn't expose that cleanly

marta: agree. i'm thinking a directed "degradation graph" where nodes are runtime modes and edges have conditions (qps, headroom, kv-cache pressure). makes reasoning/testability easier

yara: love that. also we need stable observability points at each edge so SRE can correlate what mode we were in when latency spiked (trace/span names + a metric tag).

sam: example edge metadata: condition, fallback_timeout_ms, max_batch_tokens, telemetry_tag. then the scheduler evaluates edges in priority order and plumbs tags into tracectx.

kevin: rough config proto: ```yaml
mode_nodes:
  - name: coalesce
    max_latency_ms: 40
  - name: microqueue
    max_latency_ms: 75
edges:
  - from: coalesce
    to: microqueue
    when: kv_cache_misses > 0.2 or p99_latency > 50
    telemetry_tag: "fallthrough:microqueue"
```

marta: that looks usable. couple tradeoffs: 1) static graph is easy to reason about; 2) dynamic policy (small DSL) gives more power but harder to audit. prefer explicit graph for first pass, DSL later if needed

yara: also need to define invariants: no silent starvation (tenant must either get downgraded or explicitly rate limited), and bounded oscillation (don't flip modes every 100ms). hysteresis + min dwell time required

sam: hysteresis param proposal: min_dwell_ms + exponential backoff per tenant when oscillation detected. keep defaults conservative.

kevin: question: where does the admission service live? current code has admission inside the batcher process. if we want graph evaluation and telemetry tags, maybe extract admission into an ingestable component with a small grpc API so other runtime pieces (dedicated vs hosted) can reuse it

marta: i'd prefer keeping runtime-local fast path, but move evaluation into a pluggable library. admission lib can be wired to a centralized controller in Dedicated. that avoids RPC on hot path but gives reuse.

yara: that also helps testing: we can unit test the library with synthetic metrics and ensure transitions behave. plus we can fuzz policies.

sam: testing checklist: 1) unit tests for graph transitions; 2) integration harness that replays tenant QPS traces; 3) chaos test under noisy co-tenants; 4) perf regression for happy path (coalesce)

kevin: ops concerns: need a way to force-mode for a tenant via console (debugging), and an audit log for mode transitions (tenant, prev_mode, new_mode, reason, trace_id).

marta: security note: console force-mode should be RBAC gated and write to audit log. good call.

yara: observability details: add a metric `scheduler.mode{mode="coalesce"}` as a gauge per instance + a histogram of mode-duration. traces should include `scheduler.mode` tag at root span

sam: latency accounting: when we are in degraded lanes we must surface two token-level costs: compute_tokens and quality_tokens (for billing transparency). not changing pricing now, but useful for experiments

kevin: implementation sketch: 1) admission lib exposes `EvaluateMode(tenant_metrics) -> ModeDecision` 2) batcher calls this on enqueue and on a periodic tick 3) decisions are idempotent and include a TTL so we don't evaluate too often

marta: beware of sync points: evaluation on enqueue must be fast (<1us ideally). so cache last decision per tenant and only re-evaluate on tick or when a fast signal triggers (e.g., kv cache pressure).

sam: runtime-bot: new artifact built: admission-lib v0.1.0. test-run scheduled: scheduler-compat-check tomorrow 9am PST.

kevin: followups: - draft PR for graph config shape - add telemetry hooks - plan integration tests (I can own harness)

marta: i'll write RFC followup with the graph examples and invariants. include migration plan: default config should mimic current behavior so no surprises in release

yara: last thought — graceful degradation UX for callers: include `x-runtime-mode` header on responses so app teams can know we were degraded and decide to retry with cached results if quality matters

sam: nice. small API, big win for visibility.

marta: ok i'll spin up the doc and link the admission-lib PR. thanks all. :sparkles:
